assertions.description:
During LOAD phase, each rising edge with load_en high shifts one bit MSB-first
into the 144-bit shift register {key_reg[79:0], state[63:0]}. The first bit
received becomes key_reg[79] (MSB of key) and the 144th bit received becomes
state[0] (LSB of plaintext).
assertions.name: load_shift_order

assertions.description:
Encryption begins automatically on the clock edge that accepts the 144th serial bit.
When load_cnt reaches 144 on a rising edge with load_en high, the FSM transitions
from LOAD to ENCRYPT on that same edge without requiring any additional control signal;
round counter is initialised to 1.
assertions.name: encrypt_auto_start

assertions.description:
Each encryption round applies addRoundKey, sBoxLayer, pLayer, and key schedule update
in one clock edge. Verifies the operations: XOR state with key_reg[79:16], apply S-box
to each nibble, apply pLayer permutation, update key_reg by rotating left 61 bits,
applying S-box to top nibble, and XORing round counter into bits [19:15].
assertions.name: encrypt_round_sequence

assertions.description:
After round 31 key schedule update, one additional edge applies the final addRoundKey
and asserts done. State is XORed with key_reg[79:16] (using key_reg after round-31
key schedule update), done is set to 1, and FSM transitions to DONE state.
assertions.name: final_addroundkey

assertions.description:
Once done is asserted, it remains high on every subsequent rising edge unless
rst_n is deasserted (asynchronous clear) or load_en goes high (synchronous clear
on the rising edge where load_en is first seen high in DONE state).
assertions.name: done_held

assertions.description:
dout reflects state[63] only when shift_out_en is high and done is asserted.
In DONE state, dout equals state[63] when shift_out_en is high; on each rising
edge where shift_out_en is high and done is asserted, state shifts left by one bit.
assertions.name: dout_during_unload

assertions.description:
dout is driven to 0 in all phases except active unload. Whenever the FSM is not
in DONE state, or when in DONE state but shift_out_en is low, dout must be 0.
assertions.name: dout_zero_outside_unload

assertions.description:
Asynchronous active-low reset immediately clears done and returns FSM to LOAD/IDLE.
Whenever rst_n transitions to 0, done is immediately cleared to 0, the FSM returns
to LOAD/IDLE state, load_cnt is cleared to 0, and any in-progress encryption is abandoned.
assertions.name: async_reset_effect

assertions.description:
load_cnt starts at 0 after reset; it increments by 1 on each rising edge where
load_en is high and the FSM is in LOAD state; when load_cnt reaches 144, the
ENCRYPT phase begins and load_cnt is no longer incremented.
assertions.name: load_cnt_tracking

assertions.description:
The round counter runs from 1 to 31 inclusive during ENCRYPT phase.
At the start of ENCRYPT, round is set to 1; it increments by 1 on each rising
edge in ENCRYPT state; after round 31 completes, the final addRoundKey edge
executes and the FSM moves to DONE; round never exceeds 31 during normal operation.
assertions.name: round_counter_range

assertions.description:
Key schedule rotation is a left rotation by 61 bits (equivalently right rotation
by 19 bits). key_reg[(79-61):0] becomes the new key_reg[79:19] and
key_reg[79:(80-61)] becomes the new key_reg[18:0].
assertions.name: key_schedule_rotate_left_61

rationale_notes: These assertions operate on (stim, observed) trace data where stim contains input signals
and observed contains output signals sampled each cycle. Since we only have external
port visibility (clk, rst_n, load_en, din, shift_out_en, dout, done), we must infer
internal state (key_reg, state, fsm_state, load_cnt, round) from the stimulus sequence.
For test_vector_correctness and encrypt_round_sequence we implement the full PRESENT-80
cipher in Python to cross-check. For purely observable invariants we check dout/done
against expected values derived from the stimulus trace.
The stim list contains dicts with keys: clk, rst_n, load_en, din, shift_out_en
The observed list contains dicts with keys: dout, done
We detect rising clock edges by looking at consecutive stim entries where clk goes 0->1,
but since the trace may already be sampled at rising edges only, we treat each entry
as one rising-edge sample unless clk is explicitly tracked.
